route.title: Direct when it can be. Relayed when it can't.
route.body: A relay introduces the players. etmc then tries for a direct connection, and if a network blocks it, the game carries on through the relay.
route.directNote: When the networks allow it, game traffic goes straight between players, for the lowest ping.
route.relayNote: For strict networks, like some school or mobile connections. It still works, with a little more ping.
route.diagram: Two players connected directly or through a relay

compare.title: Compare
compare.description: How etmc compares with EasyTier, ZeroTier, Tailscale, Cloudflare Mesh, Hamachi, e4mc, Essential and playit.gg.
compare.heading: How etmc compares
compare.intro: There are plenty of ways to play with friends. Here's where etmc fits, and when something else suits you better.

essential.route: Peer-to-peer, with the host as the server
essential.friends: The same mods as the host

playit.free: Free for Minecraft. Premium from $3 a month

easytier.route: Direct, or through a shared node

zerotier.route: Direct, with relaying as a fallback

hamachi.route: Direct mesh, or a central gateway

compare.checked: Checked on 5 November 2026. A dash means we couldn't confirm it from the project's own pages. Prices and limits change, so check each project's site before you decide.

picks.title: The lowest ping
picks.body: Use a tool that can connect players directly, like etmc, EasyTier, ZeroTier or Tailscale. Direct connections need networks that allow them.

picks.title: Friends who won't install anything
picks.body: Use e4mc or playit.gg, and accept higher ping. Friends join from plain Minecraft, but all traffic takes a detour through a tunnel.

picks.title: Everything inside the game
picks.body: Use etmc or Essential. There's no separate app to run. etmc also needs no account of its own.

picks.title: One network for more than Minecraft
picks.body: Use EasyTier, ZeroTier or Tailscale. They connect whole devices, so they work with other games and tools.

picks.title: No company in the middle
picks.body: Use etmc or EasyTier. Pick a community node or run your own relay, with no account to sign up for.

easytier: etmc is built on EasyTier, so they're the same network underneath. EasyTier is a general tool that you run yourself. etmc puts it inside Minecraft and handles the setup, with no adapter to create and no app to keep open.
They also work together. An etmc player can join a server that runs plain EasyTier, using a config URL.
short: Everyone needs the mod. Friends can't join from plain Minecraft.
You have to add a relay. It isn't built in, but a free community node works.
It's only for Minecraft. It won't connect anything else.
Your secret isn't protected. It's plain text, so keep it random.
compare.owners: All product names belong to their owners. etmc isn't affiliated with any of them.

generator.title: Generator
generator.description: Create a Paper server config, a player config or an etmc:// join link, or read an existing link, in your browser.
generator.intro: Create a server config or an invite link, or read a link you already have. Nothing you enter leaves your browser.
generator.paperIntro: Create the config for the etmc plugin on a Paper server.
generator.playerIntro: Create a config file for players to join from a URL.
generator.linkIntro: Create an etmc:// link from your network details.
generator.secretWarning: Your secret isn't protected. It's saved as plain text, and anyone with your link or config can read it. Keep it random, and never use a password you use anywhere else.
generator.hostKeyHint: (from /etmc status, so players can confirm it's your server)
paperSteps: Save the file as plugins/etmc/config.yml on your server.
Restart the server, or run /etmc reload.
Copy the etmc:// link from the server log, or run /etmc link.
Share the link with your players.
playerSteps: Make sure your server is on the EasyTier network at the server IP. It doesn't need etmc.
Host the file at a public HTTPS URL.
Put etmc://v1/config/ in front of the URL and share that link. Players paste it into Add Server or Direct Connect.
linkSteps: Make sure the host is reachable on the network at the server IP and port.
Send players the link. They paste it into Add Server or Direct Connect.
generator.linkNote: Anyone with the link can join, and can read the secret inside it.

config.relayIsLink: "{start}…" is an etmc join link, not a relay. A relay looks like tcp://relay.example.com:11010.
config.relayNoScheme: "{uri}" has no protocol. Write it like {example}.
config.relayBadScheme: "{scheme}://" isn't a relay protocol EasyTier knows (use tcp://, udp://, ws://, wss://, quic:// or wg://).
config.relayNoPort: "{uri}" has no port (EasyTier relays usually listen on 11010).
config.hostKeyBad: That host key isn't right. Copy it again from /etmc status.
config.relayRequired: Add at least one relay (EasyTier public node).
config.staticIpRequired: Static mode needs a client IPv4 (or switch to DHCP).
config.hostRelayRequired: Add the host's relay: without one, joiners have no way to reach the host.
config.linkIsConfig: This link loads its details from a config URL, so there's nothing in it to read.
config.linkNewer: This link needs a newer version of etmc.
config.linkInvalid: This isn't a valid etmc:// link.
config.linkDamaged: This link is damaged. Ask for a new one.
config.linkNoNetwork: This link has no network name.
